exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong aquarium proposal defends every pane of glass — here is how one student designed a classroom terrarium.

traits.sample: The outside prism is 24 in × 12 in × 16 in, so its geometric volume is 4,608 in³. Usable water would be less after freeboard, glass thickness, substrate, and equipment.
traits.why: The geometry is correct without making an unsupported animal-welfare or usable-capacity claim.

traits.trait: Counts only the glass faces needed
traits.sample: I drew and labeled a connected five-panel net with no top: 2(384) + 2(192) + 288 = 1,440 in².
traits.why: The student-drawn net is direct 6.GR.4 evidence and matches the open-top model.

traits.sample: At an illustrative $0.05 per square inch, 1,440 × 0.05 = $72 for sheet material only; safe thickness, waste, bracing, sealant, and labor are not priced.
traits.why: The cost follows from area and clearly states what the classroom estimate excludes.

traits.trait: Compares designs by cost per volume
traits.sample: My wide design costs $0.016 per cubic inch of habitat; the tall one costs $0.019 — wide wins.
traits.why: A clearly defined rate supports a level-neutral comparison when both costs include the same items.
